origin.description: Grey text that should sit behind the numbers, such as row labels and type names.
origin.details: The pillar.subtle option turns the grey on and defaults to true. An empty string is left empty. A missing value is drawn as the letters NA. With the option off, the text is unchanged and a missing value stays missing.
origin.value: A character vector of the same length.

translation.description: The same grey. None is missing. A string is one element and a list is the vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string, None, a number, or a list of those.

translation.details: pillar.subtle defaults to true. Only a real True turns the grey on. An empty string stays empty. Painting uses paste, so a missing value becomes the letters NA. With the option off, as.character is used instead, and a missing value stays missing. Set cli.num_colors first. One color pastes the text. 256 colors use the 256-color grey. Any other count uses the 16-color grey.
translation.value: A string when x is a single value, or a list when x is a list.
translation.example:
from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.num_colors": 8})

from pillar.styles import style_subtle

print(style_subtle("text"))
